Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Keep this rendering exactly as in the attached image — the same finish, line, shading, skin and colour treatment.

LEFT HAND: her own left hand stays outside the frame.

Leave behind everything she wears in the attached image — no crown, tiara, helmet, feathers, headpiece, hairpins from it, armour or regalia; her hair is styled for the everyday outfit, with at most one small accessory.

Her element — chromium: a hard, brilliant blue-white metal named from the Greek word for colour, because its compounds come in every colour — born from blood-orange crocoite crystals in Siberia, it puts the red in ruby and the green in emerald, and it became the painter's chrome yellow, chrome orange and cool viridian; plated on steel it gives a flawless mirror shine, and mixed into iron it makes stainless steel that never rusts; flamboyant, vain and dazzling, but in its hexavalent form a poison — may show in the outfit's details, motifs or small accessories.
